key_insight: Laser remelting densified detonation-sprayed NiCrFeBSiC coatings, increasing hardness and adhesion while reducing wear by 49.5%.
engineering_relevance: This combined coating process could improve wear protection for stainless-steel components in mechanical and power engineering.
method: Detonation-spray NiCrFeBSiC onto AISI 321 stainless steel, then laser-remelt.
Compare microstructure and phases using SEM, EDS, and XRD.
Evaluate indentation properties, adhesion, friction, wear, and electrochemical corrosion.
evidence_signal: Porosity fell from 0.306% to 0.15%, hardness rose from 1049.1 to 1206.1 HV, and specific wear rate decreased from 2.864 × 10⁻⁴ to 1.447 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m).
watch_item: Corrosion current density improved by only about 3%, and laser-induced coating thinning requires consideration in component design.
paper_title: Effect of Laser Remelting on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Tribological Properties of Detonation-Sprayed NiCrFeBSiC Coatings for Mechanical Engineering Applications
